say: How is the sense of self constructed?

say: The sense of self is constructed like this: when one looks into a mirror one suddenly becomes self-conscious. Even with no such notion, the moment one looks one is reminded of it, as if to exclaim: 'Ah, here I am!'

text:
The sun, the moon and the stars shine precisely because of the presence
of darkness. In the non-manifestative consciousness there is absolutely
no darkness for them to shine forth.

say: The sun, the moon and the stars shine precisely because of the presence of darkness. In the non-manifestative — with nowhere to land — consciousness there is absolutely no darkness for them to shine forth.

text:
Now that the five elements have been totally removed, the residual
function of consciousness amounts to a discrimination between the three
grades of feelings.

text:

to exist. That itself is the deliverance.

text:

assertion, 'I know, I see, it is verily so'.

text: The magical illusion created by consciousness is so complete that it is capable of playing a dual role, as in double acting. Because it reflects, like a mirror, consciousness itself is grasped, just as one grasps the mirror. Not only the reflection of the mirror, but the mirror itself is grasped.

text: Just as a dyer or a painter would fashion the likeness of a woman or of a man, complete in all its major and minor parts, on a well planed board, or a wall, or on a strip of cloth, with dye or lac or turmeric or indigo or madder, even so the untaught worldling creates, as it were, his own form, feelings, perceptions, preparations, and consciousness.

say: Just as a dyer or a painter would fashion the likeness of a woman or of a man, complete in all its major and minor parts, on a well planed board, or a wall, or on a strip of cloth, with dye or lac or turmeric or indigo or madder, even so the untaught worldling creates, as it were, his own form, pleasant-or-unpleasant tone, perceptions, things the mind makes, and consciousness.
